This reaction breaks two aldehyde C=O groups and forms the central C=C bond in a single step. Both p‑anisaldehyde molecules are commercially available and inexpensive, keeping the total cost well below $150. The retrosynthesis tree therefore has the target molecule as the root, a single reaction node (McMurry coupling), and two identical leaf nodes representing p‑anisaldehyde.</thought>
